headline: Gemini with Google Sheets eliminates the need for multiple productivity apps
summary: Google Sheets, powered by Gemini, now simplifies complex spreadsheet creation, enabling users to build custom trackers and planners with plain English prompts. This integration can replace numerous dedicated productivity apps.
details: Gemini's integration into Google Sheets is transforming how users approach productivity, allowing them to create sophisticated spreadsheets by simply describing their needs in plain English. This capability can replace the need for multiple dedicated apps for budgeting, meal planning, project tracking, and more.

Traditionally, building custom spreadsheets involved time-consuming manual tasks like structuring, creating columns, writing formulas, adding dropdowns, applying conditional formatting, and building charts. Even simple trackers could take too long to set up, deterring many users.

Gemini removes this busywork, enabling users to prompt the AI to create monthly budgets with automatic totals and charts, build project trackers with status dropdowns, generate formulas for expense calculation, summarize data trends, or even troubleshoot non-working formulas.

It can also efficiently create pivot tables, apply conditional formatting, build charts, and organize data without requiring users to remember complex options or functions. Access to this feature is available to eligible Google Workspace customers and Google AI plan subscribers.

Users can access Gemini by opening a spreadsheet and clicking the 'Ask Gemini' button, then choosing a suggested prompt or describing their requirements. The AI then generates the requested tables, formulas, charts, or edits directly within the spreadsheet.

For instance, the author used Gemini to create a detailed monthly budget tracker and a comprehensive travel planner, customizing them with specific requirements. Gemini can modify existing sheets, add new tables or formulas, and create charts as needs evolve.

This makes Google Sheets feel like a personalized app, adapting to individual organizing styles for various tasks. Gemini also assists with complex formulas by generating them, explaining their functionality, and troubleshooting errors, making advanced spreadsheet use more accessible.
caption:

headline: Lost $2,000 ebike leads to months of chatbot hell for frustrated customer
summary: A customer's missing $2,000 ebike delivery sparked a monthslong ordeal, forcing them to navigate multiple AI-driven customer service systems without human assistance. This highlights a growing frustration with AI in support roles.
details: A customer's new $2,000 ebike went missing after FedEx claimed it was delivered and signed for by an unknown "M.M." This unexpected delivery failure initiated a frustrating, monthslong quest for resolution.

The customer faced an endless loop of AI chatbots across FedEx, the bike retailer, their bank, credit card company, and even the local police department. Despite hours spent, finding a real human to address the issue proved nearly impossible.

This experience reflects a broader trend where corporations increasingly deploy AI in customer service, often reducing human staff. A recent survey found 31% of customer service leaders plan to cut headcount due to AI adoption.

Experts note that AI has amplified "sludge" tactics, where companies intentionally make resolution difficult to discourage customers. This leads to a more acute version of long wait times and non-answers.
Consumer sentiment is clear: a May report showed 59% of US, UK, and Canadian consumers are frustrated with AI customer service agents. A significant 85% prefer speaking with a real person.

The customer eventually got FedEx to open a claim, only to receive an automated email stating the bike was missing and they needed to contact the shipper for restitution, continuing the cycle of frustration.
